title: OmniStudio Developer Certification — Practice Quiz
description: Five questions drawn from the first three OmniStudio exam-guide requirements (F-1, F-2, F-3). Pick the best answer, then read the explanation.

questions.question: Which DataRaptor operation is used to write data into Salesforce?
options: DataRaptor Extract
DataRaptor Transform
DataRaptor Load
DataRaptor Turbo Extract
questions.explanation: DataRaptor Load writes transformed data back into Salesforce objects — Extract and Transform only read/reshape data, and Turbo Extract is a read-optimized variant.

questions.question: An OmniStudio solution for a healthcare payer must surface patient eligibility across multiple downstream systems. What is the standard pattern for pulling that data together?
options: DataRaptor Load into a staging object, then Apex triggers to fan out
DataRaptor Turbo Extract for high-volume reads, composed in an OmniScript
A single OmniScript with the data entered manually by the agent
A FlexCard that calls each system over external services individually
questions.explanation: Turbo Extract is the read-optimized DataRaptor for high-volume, low-latency data pulls; an OmniScript orchestrates the extraction and presents it to the agent. Manual entry and per-system FlexCards defeat the point of an integrated solution.

questions.question: In requirement F-2, a project's needs are determined by evaluating which four inputs?
options: Requirements, assumptions, risks, and constraints
Features, costs, timelines, and stakeholders
User stories, acceptance criteria, epics, and sprints
Integration points, data volumes, licenses, and security
questions.explanation: F-2 is: 'Determine a project's needs by evaluating a customer's requirements, assumptions, risks, and constraints.' The other groupings mix in execution concerns (sprints, costs) that belong to later phases.

questions.question: A customer wants their OmniStudio deployment upgraded automatically when Salesforce releases a new version. Which runtime supports that?
options: Managed Package Runtime
Standard Runtime
Legacy Runtime
Custom Runtime
questions.explanation: Managed Package Runtime is the release vehicle for OmniStudio — automatic upgrades flow through the managed package on the Salesforce release cadence. Standard Runtime is for installed, non-package-managed metadata.

questions.question: Which statement best describes how OmniStudio components (OmniScripts, FlexCards, DataRaptors) are organized and delivered?
options: Each component ships independently and is installed one at a time
Components are grouped into OmniStudio applications that package the related pieces together
All components must live in a single unmanaged project with no grouping
Components are only delivered through Apex classes compiled at deploy time
questions.explanation: OmniStudio organizes related components into applications — a package-like grouping of OmniScripts, FlexCards, DataRaptors, and other elements that can be moved and deployed together. This is core to how OmniStudio solutions are structured.
